cohort_total_n_excerpt: Dietary indicators of prostatic cancer risk were analyzed in a case-control study conducted in Northern Italy on 96 histologically confirmed cases and 292 controls in hospital for acute, nonneoplastic or genital tract diseases.
reason: The abstract evaluates prostate cancer cases overall and does not analyze an aggressive, advanced, metastatic, high-grade, high-risk, or lethal incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: There was a significant trend in risk as regards frequency of milk consumption: compared with nondrinkers or occasional milk drinkers, the relative risk (RR) was 1.2 (95% confidence interval, Cl, 0.7-1.9) for 1 or 2 glasses per day and 5.0 (95% Cl 1.5-16.6) for 2 or more glasses per day.
estimate_classifications.reason: The milk estimate concerns prostate cancer overall; no aggressive subtype is identified.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: However, the interpretation of these findings is not clear, since other sources of animal fat, like eggs or meat, as well as a summary fat score, were unrelated to prostatic cancer.
estimate_classifications.reason: The egg association concerns prostate cancer overall and has no aggressive endpoint designation.
